chunks: Ahmad ibn Ziyad ibn Ja'far al-Hamadani (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Ali ibn Ibrahim narrated to us from his father Ibrahim ibn Hashim, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Abu Ayyub al-Khazzaz, from Abu Basir, from Abu Abdillah al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father, from his forefathers (peace be upon them), from Abu Dharr (may God have mercy on him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (may God bless him and his family) said:
The longest of you in qunut in this world will be the most restful of you on the Day of Resurrection at the Stand.

key_terms.الموقف: Al-Mawqif - the Stand, the gathering place on the Day of Judgment
key_terms.قنوت: Qunut - prolonged devotional standing in prayer, humble supplication

ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet Muhammad say about the benefit of qunut in prayer?
ai.summary: This hadith transmits a prophetic saying through Abu Dharr al-Ghifari via Imam al-Sadiq (AS) and his forefathers. The Prophet (S) establishes a direct correlation between devotional standing (qunut) in this worldly life and comfort on the Day of Judgment. The term 'qunut' encompasses humble, prolonged supplication during prayer. For the original audience of early Muslims, this was practical encouragement to invest in night prayers and extended supplication.

en.bilal-muhammad: Ahmad b. Ziyad b. Ja`far al-Hamadani (ra) narrated to us. He said: `Ali b. Ibrahim narrated to us from his father Ibrahim b. Hashim from Safwan b. Yahya from Abi Ayyub al-Khazzaz from Abi Basir from Abi `Abdillah al-Sadiq Ja`far b. Muhammad from his father from his forefathers (as) from Abi Dharr (rh). He said: The Messenger of Allah (s) said:
The longest of you in qunut in this world will be the most restful of you on the Day of Resurrection at the stand.
